source: USCIS Vocabulary for the Naturalization Interview: Self-Test 2
privacy_note: No personal information. Generic USCIS practice vocabulary only.

key_words.example: Michael is habitually late for work at the bank.
Can you verify this information?
What is your marital status?
I swear to tell the truth.
John registered for an English class.
Did your spouse travel with you?
What is your current home address?
What is your date of birth?
Mary advocated to change working conditions.
Jim failed to send in his taxes on time.
Is that a federal government building?

key_words.meaning: to not have to do something
key_words.example: Donna was exempt from the final exam.
Gary has prior experience teaching history.
The decision is pending.
Have you ever visited New York?
Scott is a member of an organization.

key_words.meaning: someone who lives in a place
key_words.example: I am a resident of Texas.
John requested information.
Barbara's disability made walking difficult.
Do you have any dependents?

multiple_choice.question: habitually — Michael is habitually late for work at the bank.
choices: Michael is never late for work at the bank.
Michael is often late for work at the bank.
Michael was late for work at the bank yesterday.
multiple_choice.answer: Michael is often late for work at the bank.

multiple_choice.question: verify — Can you verify this information?
choices: Can you prove that this information is true?
multiple_choice.answer: Can you prove that this information is true?

multiple_choice.question: marital status — What is your marital status?
choices: When were you married to your spouse?
Whom are you married to now?
Are you married, divorced, single, or widowed now?
multiple_choice.answer: Are you married, divorced, single, or widowed now?

multiple_choice.question: swear — I swear to tell the truth.
choices: I like to tell the truth.
I promise to tell the truth.
I forget to tell the truth.
multiple_choice.answer: I promise to tell the truth.

multiple_choice.question: registered — John registered for an English class.
choices: John signed up for an English class.
multiple_choice.answer: John signed up for an English class.

multiple_choice.question: spouse — Did your spouse go with you?
choices: Did your husband or wife go with you?
Did your children go with you?
Did other people go with you?
multiple_choice.answer: Did your husband or wife go with you?

multiple_choice.question: current home address — What is your current home address?
multiple_choice.answer: Where do you live now?

multiple_choice.question: date of birth — What is your date of birth?
multiple_choice.answer: When were you born?

multiple_choice.question: advocated — Mary advocated to change working conditions.
multiple_choice.answer: Mary supported a change.

multiple_choice.question: failed to — Jim failed to send in his taxes on time.
choices: Jim did not send taxes on time.
multiple_choice.answer: Jim did not send taxes on time.

multiple_choice.question: federal — Is that a federal government building?
choices: Is that a U.S. government building?
multiple_choice.answer: Is that a U.S. government building?

multiple_choice.question: exempt — Donna was exempt from the final exam.
choices: Donna did not have to take the exam.
multiple_choice.answer: Donna did not have to take the exam.

multiple_choice.question: prior — Gary has prior experience teaching history.
multiple_choice.answer: Gary has taught history before.

multiple_choice.question: pending — The decision is pending.
choices: It has not been decided yet.
multiple_choice.answer: It has not been decided yet.

multiple_choice.question: Have you ever — Have you ever visited New York?
choices: In your lifetime, have you visited New York?
Are you planning to visit New York?
Will you visit New York next summer?
multiple_choice.answer: In your lifetime, have you visited New York?

multiple_choice.question: member — Scott is a member of an organization.
multiple_choice.answer: Scott belongs to it.

multiple_choice.question: resident — I am a resident of Texas.
multiple_choice.answer: I live in Texas now.

multiple_choice.question: requested — John requested information.
multiple_choice.answer: John asked for information.

multiple_choice.question: disability — Barbara's disability made walking difficult.
choices: Barbara did not like to walk.
multiple_choice.answer: Barbara had a physical impairment.

multiple_choice.question: dependents — Do you have any dependents?
multiple_choice.answer: Do you support anyone financially?

definitions: often, frequent, or doing something from habit
officially sign up or put your name on a list
ask for something formally or politely
publicly support an idea or person
whether you are single, married, divorced, or widowed
have special permission to not do something
a physical or mental condition that limits one or more major life activities
month, day, and year that a person was born
someone who depends on you for food, clothes, money, etc.

answers.request: ask for something formally or politely
answers.exempt: have special permission to not do something
answers.date of birth: month, day, and year that a person was born
answers.habitual: often, frequent, or doing something from habit
answers.disability: a physical or mental condition that limits one or more major life activities
answers.advocate: publicly support an idea or person
answers.dependent: someone who depends on you for food, clothes, money, etc.
answers.marital status: whether you are single, married, divorced, or widowed
answers.register: officially sign up or put your name on a list
